newsitem.title: THAILAND: Some Thai sugar mills delay crushing -- official.
newsitem.headline: Some Thai sugar mills delay crushing -- official.

text.p: Only three out of 11 sugar mills in northeastern Thailand have started sugarcane crushing since crushing was set to begin on November 5, an official at the Sugar Board said on Monday.
The delay was caused by the upcoming general election, local festivals and some factories not being ready, the official told Reuters.
Thailand's crushing season normally starts in November and ends in late May or early June. There are 46 sugar mills registered in the country.

"We received letters from some factories, notifying us of the delay," the official said. "Reasons ranged from festivities in some areas, to the election, to their staff not being ready. Many said they want to start crushing after the election," she said. The mills did not elaborate why staff were not ready, she added.
A general election is scheduled for November 17 in Thailand.
The three mills currently in operation were Khon Kaen, Kasetphol and Kumpawapee, the official said.

According to the 1996/97 crushing schedule set by a committee comprising government officials, millers and sugarcane farmers, mills in northeastern Thailand were due to start crushing first, beginning on November 5.
The 19 mills in central Thailand have different crushing schedules. The crushing will start from November 25, December 8, December 17 and December 23, depending on their locations.

The 10 crushing mills in the north will run their factories from December 4 and six factories in the east will start on November 20. The schedule is usually based on weather conditions and the preparedness of the mills.
Normally, the mills must operate within seven days after the starting date and must notify officials if they fail to do so.

The Sugar Board forecast that 60.32 million tonnes of cane would be crushed for 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) to produce 6.28 million tonnes tel quel for sugar output compared with 57.69 million tonnes of cane crushed to produce 6.03 million tonnes on sugar in 1995/96.
